title: Salesforce Platform Events Architecture and Patterns
summary: Platform Events provide an event-driven architecture on the Salesforce platform using a publish-subscribe model. Events are defined with the __e suffix, support custom fields (Checkbox, Date, DateTime, Number, Text, Text Area Long), and include a system-generated ReplayId for event replay. Events are NOT transactional — they cannot be rolled back and are not part of database transactions.

findings.event_definition: Platform events are defined similar to custom objects but use the __e suffix. Each event supports custom fields of types: Checkbox, Date, DateTime, Number, Text, and Text Area Long. A system field ReplayId is automatically assigned to each published event for ordering and replay.
findings.publishing_mechanisms: Events can be published through four mechanisms: (1) Apex using EventBus.publish(), (2) Process Builder, (3) Flow, and (4) REST/SOAP API. Apex publishing supports batch operations and returns SaveResult for error handling.
findings.subscription_patterns: Two primary subscription patterns: (1) Apex Triggers — fire on event receipt with support for EventBus.RetryableException for transient failure recovery, and (2) CometD streaming API — enables external system subscription using long-polling. CometD subscribers use ReplayId to resume from a specific point in the event stream.
findings.transaction_isolation: Platform events are explicitly outside database transactions. A published event cannot be rolled back even if the publishing transaction fails. This means event publishing should be the last operation in a transaction, or the receiving system must handle idempotency.
findings.migration_support: Platform event definitions can be managed through Metadata API, enabling deployment across environments via change sets or CI/CD pipelines.

source: Salesforce Platform Events Developer Guide — Summer '17 (API v40.0)
